description: Cloudflare Containers topology for Vigil's Python tier. Single source of truth for which Python processes run as Containers, from which image, with which ports, lifecycle and state. The deploy half of workstream F renders wrangler's containers[] / durable_objects.bindings[] / migrations[] from this file; tests/unit/infra/test_cloudflare_python_tier.py asserts it against the repo so the two cannot drift.

image_build.note: Both Dockerfiles COPY from the repo root (core/, services/, mempalace/, VERSION), so the build context is the repo root -- not the Dockerfile's own directory. Images are therefore built and pushed by CI (docker build -f infra/docker/Dockerfile.backend .) and referenced from wrangler by fully-qualified image reference. Pointing wrangler's `image` at a Dockerfile path would hand the build a context that cannot satisfy those COPY lines.

containers.name: vigil-api
containers.keep_alive_note: Request-driven: every API call resets the activity timer, and an idle instance may sleep. Cold start costs one image start (~1-3s per Cloudflare's lifecycle docs).

containers.name: vigil-daemon
containers.singleton_note: The daemon owns three unbounded loops, the Splunk/CrowdStrike pollers, the sandbox submit/poll cycle and the Kafka consumer-group member, all in one process (services/daemon/main.py). A second instance would double-poll every source and take a second seat in the consumer group, so max_instances is pinned to 1 -- the Containers equivalent of the legacy single-replica StatefulSet.
containers.keep_alive_note: The daemon's work is background work: nothing arrives on its ports between webhooks, so request activity cannot keep it awake. The Worker must ping health_port on a cron trigger (interval < sleep_after) so the activity timer is renewed. Without that ping the loops stop at sleep_after and only restart on the next inbound webhook.

containers.name: vigil-llm-worker
containers.keep_alive_note: ARQ worker: it drains the Redis queue and serves no port, so it is started explicitly (Container.start) and kept awake by the same cron trigger as the daemon. Included because the API enqueues every LLM request here -- an API container without a drained queue answers requests it never completes.
containers.entrypoint_note: Mirrors the llm-worker command in infra/docker/docker-compose.yml: same image as the API, different command.

external_services.placement_rationale: Postgres, Redis and Kafka stay outside Cloudflare Containers. Two documented platform properties decide it: end users (and peers) cannot open non-HTTP TCP or UDP connections to a Container -- every request enters through a Worker -- and all Container disk is ephemeral, so a stopped instance restarts with a fresh disk from its image. A database that cannot be reached over its wire protocol and cannot keep its data files is not a database. They run as managed services reachable outbound from both the edge and the Python tier.

postgres.note: findings.embedding is vector(768) with an HNSW index, so the instance must ship the pgvector extension (the compose default is pgvector/pgvector:pg16). The Python tier dials it directly on 5432; the edge reaches the same database through Hyperdrive, which is the deploy half's concern.

redis.note: ARQ queue plus session store. Only the Python tier speaks Redis; the edge does not.

kafka.note: Kafka is usually the customer's own broker, and Vigil is a consumer-group member, so the only requirement is outbound connectivity from the daemon container (Containers have outbound internet by default). Nothing dials into Vigil, which is what makes this workload viable on the platform at all.

state.note: Open: the legacy daemon mounts a 10Gi ReadWriteOnce PVC at /app/data/investigations. Cloudflare Container disk is ephemeral -- a restarted instance gets a fresh disk from the image -- so there is no direct PVC equivalent, and the honest options are the instance disk (default here: fast, sized by instance_type, lost on restart) or an R2 bucket mounted over FUSE (durable, and explicitly not SSD-speed per Cloudflare's docs). Which one ships depends on the stateDirectory inventory (spec open question 2): if the workdir only holds in-flight investigation artifacts that a restart can rebuild, ephemeral-disk is correct; if anything under it is the only copy, r2-fuse is required. Both stay configurable via the env vars above until the inventory answers it.

telemetry.note: Containers export traces to an external OTLP endpoint over TLS with auth headers; there is no in-cluster collector to fall back on. The compose observability profile (collector, Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana) is a local development convenience only.
